Backend: 14/14 iter33 sprint tests PASS in isolation (verify-email single-use, /me/export bundle w/ 8 sections, /me/delete-request+DELETE anonymises PII, forgot-password rate-limit 429 on 4th call, hardcoded-password lint exit 0, SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD prod-only helper, deploy_precheck blocks unset SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD). Regression: 53/55 across iter30/31/32/33 sprint suites when run in one shot — the 2 failures are iter32 forgot-password tests hitting 429 due to persistent in-memory rate-limit state from earlier iter33 test run; re-verified they PASS 2/2 after backend restart (real bug in RL is NOT present, this is expected in-mem RL state carry-over between test invocations). Frontend E2E on preview URL: (1) /preferences renders email-verification-card ONLY when user.email_verified=false — hidden for learner (verified=true) [both branches confirmed]; (2) Resend link button POSTs /api/auth/resend-verification and toasts 'Verification email queued'; (3) Download my data streams a JSON file (`ifpi-data-export-YYYY-MM-DD.json`) containing profile/enrollments/exam_attempts/certificates/notifications/audit_records/active_sessions — profile.email matches session user; (4) Delete-account confirm dialog opens, Cancel button aborts safely; (5) After 'Send code', prompt dialog for 6-digit code appears; wrong code (999999) triggers backend 400 + red toast; (6) /verify-email/bogus-token renders error card with 'Verification failed'; (7) /verify-email/<valid-token> — backend correctly sets users.email_verified_at, but the UI shows the ERROR card because React.StrictMode double-invokes the useEffect in dev/preview builds, so the second call gets a 400 (token already used) and overwrites the success state. Prod build (StrictMode effect double-run is dev-only) will not exhibit this, but the frontend should guard with a useRef anyway.

minor.issue: In-memory rate-limit state persists across pytest invocations against the same running backend, causing false test-suite failures when iter33's intentional-exhaust test (test_forgot_password_rate_limit_by_email) runs before iter32's 200-response tests. Not a production bug — expected RL behaviour. Consider adding an ADMIN/test-only /api/rate-limit/reset endpoint or a pytest fixture that resets rate_limit_service._mem_buckets in the backend process.

ui_bugs.issue: React.StrictMode double-invokes the useEffect on mount in dev/preview builds, calling /api/auth/verify-email twice. First call succeeds (200, token consumed, users.email_verified_at set), second call gets 400 'Verification link already used' and overwrites the state to 'error', so the user sees a 'Verification failed' card even though verification succeeded. Fix: guard with a useRef so the effect runs at most once, or use an AbortController.

action_items: VerifyEmailPage.tsx — Guard the verify-email POST with a useRef so React StrictMode double-invoke doesn't consume the token twice and leave the UI showing an error after a successful verification. Suggested pattern: `const done = useRef(false); useEffect(() => { if (done.current) return; done.current = true; api.post(...) })`.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 33 GDPR sprint is 99% green. rca of the issue: VerifyEmailPage.tsx (line 22-35): the useEffect that calls `api.post('/auth/verify-email', {token})` has no guard against React.StrictMode's intentional double-invoke of effects in dev mode. Sequence: mount → useEffect runs once (verifies token, sets state='ok') → StrictMode unmounts/remounts to test resilience → useEffect runs again (400 from backend, sets state='error'). Backend verification succeeded; only the final UI state is wrong. Fix: `const attempted = useRef(false); useEffect(() => { if (attempted.current || !token) return; attempted.current = true; api.post(...) }, [token])`. Alternate: distinguish the 'already verified' error server-side and treat it as success client-side.
